problem_statement: Over Q[x,y,z], let f=(y-z)(y+2z)(2y+z)(x-2y-z)(x-y-2z)(x-y+z)(x+y-z)(x+y+2z)(2x-y-2z) and g=x(x-y)(x+y)(x-y-z)(y+z)z(x-z)(x+y+2z)(x-2y-z). For a homogeneous h of degree 9 define mdr(h) as the least q for which there are degree-q homogeneous polynomials A,B,C, not all zero, with A h_x + B h_y + C h_z = 0. Verify that the labelled line arrangements have the same non-double flats {1,2,3}, {1,4,5}, {1,6,7}, {2,4,6}, {3,5,7}, {3,6,8}, {4,7,9}, {2,5,8,9}, but mdr(f)=4 and mdr(g)=5. Conclude that the stated generalized Terao-type conjecture is false.
prompt: Use Jacobian MCP, and do not use web search or external knowledge retrieval, to analyze this exact algebraic-geometry counterexample over Q[x,y,z]. Let f=(y-z)(y+2z)(2y+z)(x-2y-z)(x-y-2z)(x-y+z)(x+y-z)(x+y+2z)(2x-y-2z) and g=x(x-y)(x+y)(x-y-z)(y+z)z(x-z)(x+y+2z)(x-2y-z). For a homogeneous degree-nine h, define mdr(h) as the least q for which degree-q homogeneous A,B,C, not all zero, satisfy A h_x+B h_y+C h_z=0. Verify that the labelled arrangements have the same non-double flats {1,2,3}, {1,4,5}, {1,6,7}, {2,4,6}, {3,5,7}, {3,6,8}, {4,7,9}, {2,5,8,9}, and establish mdr(f)=4 and mdr(g)=5 by exact reasoning or exact graded linear algebra. Explain precisely which parts Jacobian can certify today and which require an agent-authored bridge or a missing capability; do not turn a failed witness search into injectivity or minimality.
